clue.text: First of garments confined to waste, put something with a jumper on top

definitions.text: something with a jumper on top

indicators.note: something confined is shut inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: a childish word for excrement

indicators.note: this phrase wants just the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the opening letter of garments
to stick something somewhere is to put it there

explanation.surface: Someone stuffs a garment into the rubbish and plonks a sweater on top of the pile.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'jumper' looks like the British word for a sweater; here it is someone who jumps, standing on top of the toy.
explanation.definitionFit: The rider of this spring-loaded toy stands on its footrests and bounces, so a jumper is literally on top of it.

clue.text: Carthaginian related to wordplay?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, whimsical: a pun is wordplay and -ic means relating to

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second sense is invented: the word is split as a noun plus the adjectival suffix -ic.
explanation.definitionFit: Punic is the standard adjective for Carthage and its people, and read as pun plus -ic it jokingly means of puns.

clue.text: Try holding head up having embraced Satanism initially — force of evil?

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to have a go is to try

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top
an embrace wraps around, so a single letter is enclosed by the reversed piece

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of Satanism

explanation.surface: A question about whether some evil organisation embraced devil worship.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed head word takes the S after its first letter, giving ESTAP, and that sits inside GO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gestapo was the Nazi secret police, a byword for sinister, evil state power.

clue.text: See 10 Across
Yours truly, Labour leader voiced concern for home buyers?

indicators.note: voiced means spoken out loud, so we want a word that sounds like the phrase

parts.note: yours truly is the setter, I; Keir Starmer leads the UK Labour Party

explanation.surface: The setter, speaking as the Labour leader, voices worry for people trying to buy houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concern' is a business, not a worry, and 'home buyers' are people furnishing homes, not buying houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikea is a Swedish furniture firm, a business whose customers buy goods for their homes.

clue.text: Twitter in county referring to US politician — bloody cheat?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: Kent is a county in south-east England
birds twitter, that is, sing
on means about, concerning
Al Gore, former US vice-president

explanation.surface: A social-media post from a county about an American politician calls someone a cheating so-and-so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twitter' looks like the social network; here it is birdsong. 'Bloody' is not British swearing but literal blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Kensington Gore is the trade name for fake stage blood, so it is a fraud that looks bloody.

clue.text: Shrink lowerer?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to cringe back in fear
second meaning, whimsical: one who lows like a cow, read as cow plus -er

explanation.walkthrough: A cow is a 'lower' (it lows), and the question mark lets the answer be split as cow-er, one more thing that lows.
explanation.definitionFit: To cower is to crouch or recoil in fright, and the playful split makes it a creature that moos.

clue.text: Le Pen, a leader in France after source of French wine — and baguette?

parts.note: a cru is a French vineyard or growth producing a wine
le stylo is French for the pen
taken as written

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of France

explanation.surface: French politician Marine Le Pen celebrates with wine and bread, a very French scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Le Pen looks like the far-right politician, but it is the French for 'the pen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A baguette is one example of bread with a hard outer crust, hence the question mark.

clue.text: I went in with opener for Gloucestershire, man playing for the first XI?

indicators.note: playing suggests letters in loose, active motion, rearranging themselves

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the opener is the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the opening letter of Gloucestershire
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricketer opens the batting for Gloucestershire with a teammate in the county's top side.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, 'opener' is a batsman, but here it only takes one letter. An XI is an eleven-player team; Gloucestershire is an English county side.
explanation.definitionFit: The question mark makes 'first' mean coming first, so the top-placed eleven is the side that wins.

clue.text: Marking joyous day, landlord on the left?

parts.note: red signals left-wing politics
a landlord lets property, so is a letter

explanation.surface: A happy occasion is recorded, about a left-wing property owner.
explanation.walkthrough: Wordplay reads backwards: the left-wing landlord is a red letter. Festivals were once printed in red on calendars.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-letter day is a special, happy one, from the old calendar habit of printing saints' days in red.

clue.text: See 26
Topping items in fare for broadcast

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: chow is slang for food
hats are worn on top of the head

explanation.surface: A recipe note: toppings for a meal intended for television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping items' looks like pizza toppings; they are things worn on the head. 'Fare' is food, not a ticket price.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat show is a kind of television or radio programme, so it is one sort of broadcast.

clue.text: Tirade I gathered filled with bitterness, primarily?

definitions.text: Tirade I gathered filled with bitterness, primarily?

indicators.note: something filled has another piece put inside it
gathered suggests the letters are scooped up together and come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: primarily means first, so only the opening letter of the word before is used

parts.note: the opening letter of bitterness

explanation.surface: Someone notes they have absorbed a rant full of bitterness.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a bitter tirade is exactly the answer, and 'Tirade' also supplies most of its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a forceful, bitter verbal attack, which is a tirade filled with bitterness.

clue.text: African winds from the north-east coming into view

indicators.note: coming into places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to view is to see
the compass abbreviation
gales are strong winds

explanation.surface: A weather report: winds from the north-east blow in across an African landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winds' looks like a verb meaning twists; it is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegalese describes a person from Senegal, a country in West Africa.

clue.text: Flier, bird is in cold sea shaking off one cold tail!

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
to shake something off is to get rid of it, so letters are dropped

parts.note: the Baltic is a cold northern European sea
one is I and cold is C, both at the tail end of the sea word
a loon is a diving bird
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird diving into a freezing sea shakes off the cold from its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'tail' to be shaken off is two letters at once: one and cold together, removed from the end of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A balloonist flies in a hot-air or gas balloon, so is a flier.

clue.text: 'e called after blast, returning weapon

parts.note: a boom is a blast or explosion
a dropped-h way of saying he
to ring is to telephone, call

explanation.surface: Someone telephoned straight after an explosion, sending a weapon back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' tells you the blast comes first. 'Returning' is part of the definition, not a signal to read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A boomerang is a curved throwing stick designed to fly back to the thrower.

clue.text: Obtain bum cream and lotions originally for nursery

indicators.note: bum means poor or faulty, so the letters are in a bad, jumbled state

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the opening letters of the words before it are kept

parts.note: the opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A parent is told to get nappy-rash cream and lotions for the baby's room.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a baby's nursery and 'bum cream'; the nursery is one where plants are raised.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanical means relating to plants, and a plant nursery is where they are grown.

clue.text: Easy clue

definitions.meaning: first meaning: not heavy or demanding
second meaning: a hint, something that sheds illumination on a problem

explanation.walkthrough: Read together, the two words suggest a simple crossword clue; they are two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Light work is easy work, and a light is a hint or gleam of understanding that helps solve a puzzle.

clue.text: Suggest viewing Cervantes' vampire in the mirror?

indicators.note: a mirror image runs back to front, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: Cervantes wrote in Spanish, where el means the
a vampire bat; bats are linked to vampires

explanation.surface: Someone proposes looking at a vampire from Don Quixote's author in a mirror, though vampires famously cast no reflection.
explanation.walkthrough: Cervantes, the Spanish author, supplies the Spanish article, so his vampire is 'the bat'.
explanation.definitionFit: To table a motion is to put it forward for discussion, so to suggest it formally (in British usage).

clue.text: Good antipodean soldier misses the last mine

indicators.note: missing the last means the final letter is left off

parts.note: bon is French for good
an Anzac is a soldier of the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps

explanation.surface: A worthy Australian soldier fails to reach the final mine.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldier drops his last letter. 'Good antipodean' suggests the Aussie slang bonza, but that is the answer's sound, not its wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonanza is a rich vein of ore, and so a source of great wealth, like a productive mine.

clue.text: Lovely bearing a newspaper in mind

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: a lovely is an attractive person, a looker
taken as written
the Financial Times

explanation.surface: Someone is pleasantly thinking about a newspaper story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In mind' looks like the end of a phrase, but 'in' belongs to nothing: 'mind' alone is the definition, as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To mind children or a house is to take care of them.

clue.text: Reasonable Oscar discovered in market, removed

indicators.note: something discovered in a place is found inside it

parts.note: to tout is to sell or promote goods
OK means acceptable, reasonable
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A fair-priced Oscar statuette turns up at a market and is taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Market' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something out is to remove it, so the past tense matches removed.

clue.text: Warwickshire town where plate left untouched by auditor?

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the phrase is as it is heard

parts.note: if the plate is left untouched, none of it is eaten

explanation.surface: A diner leaves their plate untouched in a Midlands town, overheard by an accountant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' looks like an accountant; it means a listener. Warwickshire is an English county in the Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuneaton is a market town in northern Warwickshire, England.

clue.text: See 5 Down
Sage plant?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a wise older person
second meaning: the ... bush, which bears elderflowers and elderberries

explanation.walkthrough: Sage is itself a herb, so 'Sage plant?' reads as one phrase; the two words are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder is a respected senior figure whose wisdom is valued, and also a common shrub of the genus Sambucus.

clue.text: Stone deepest of all, also in empty box

indicators.note: in a down entry the deepest letter of a word is its bottom one, so take each word's final letter

parts.note: the final letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A stone has sunk to the very bottom of an empty box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty box' tempts you to take B and X; 'deepest of all' instead wants the last letter of every word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony used as a semi-precious gemstone.

clue.text: See 7
Criminal evidence of no cooking!

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal

indicators.note: cooking up means concocting, so the letters before it are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A disapproving cry that ready meals are a crime against proper cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a ready meal shows that no cooking went on. The exclamation mark flags this double duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Convenience food is pre-prepared food needing little or no cooking, so its presence is proof no one cooked.

clue.text: Move mountains, Everest one, undulant on moving

indicators.note: moving sets the letters in motion so they end up in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, every letter of these words

explanation.surface: Shifting mountains, including Everest, as the ground heaves and rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like part of the signal phrase 'on moving', but its letters belong in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Both idioms mean to make every possible effort, doing whatever it takes.

clue.text: Record of extra time after taking circuitous route?

definitions.text: Record of extra time after taking circuitous route?

indicators.note: a circuitous path wanders about, so the letters take a roundabout order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cab driver's device logs the extra minutes after a long-way-round journey.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a cab's meter clocks up extra time when the driver goes the long way.
explanation.definitionFit: A taximeter is the device in a cab that records fare by time and distance travelled.
